titre: Knorozov and the Syllabic Reading of Maya Writing
accroche: In 1952, a thirty-year-old Soviet linguist claims Maya glyphs read as syllables. The field's leading authority judges him for twenty years.
contenu_vulgarise:
In 1952, in the Soviet journal *Sovetskaya Etnografiya*, a young researcher at the Moscow Institute of Ethnography, Yuri Knorozov, argues that Maya writing isn't made only of symbols standing for whole words, but also of syllabic signs, each for a consonant followed by a vowel. His starting point is a sixteenth-century document left unused for decades: in his *Relación de las cosas de Yucatán*, the Spanish bishop Diego de Landa had recorded a Maya "alphabet," matched letter for letter against the Latin alphabet, which specialists judged incomprehensible or invented. Knorozov proposes reading it differently: each sign in Landa's list doesn't correspond to an isolated letter, but to a syllable, and the Maya scribe who dictated this glossary to Landa, not knowing the Spanish names of the letters, simply pronounced the sound each letter makes in Spanish, heard as a Maya syllable.

## Twenty Years of Opposition

The hypothesis meets the opposition of the British archaeologist J. Eric S. Thompson, who had already called Landa's glossary nonsense in 1950, and whose authority then dominates Maya studies. For two decades, few researchers dare publicly oppose him, and the syllabic reading stays marginal, held back also by distrust of a Soviet author in the middle of the Cold War. Knorozov keeps going nonetheless, and publishes in 1956, in the *Journal de la Société des Américanistes*, an article that takes up and refines the reading of Landa's alphabet, glyph by glyph, with several examples of syllabic breakdown, presented that same year at the 32nd International Congress of Americanists, in Copenhagen.

## The Turning Point

The turning point comes from different ground: in the 1960s, the epigrapher Tatiana Proskouriakoff shows that the inscriptions on Maya stelae aren't only ritual or astronomical texts, but record dated events, births, accessions, wars of identifiable rulers. In December 1973, at the first Palenque Round Table, a team of researchers using the syllabic approach reconstructs, in a single afternoon, most of the dynastic list of that city's kings. From that point on, epigraphic work grounded in the syllabic reading multiplies rapidly. Thompson dies in 1975.

## What This Shifts

Maya writing turned out to be mixed, logograms and syllables combined within the same text, which explains why an all-one-or-all-the-other reading had failed for decades. And the episode is a reminder that a correct hypothesis can stay set aside for twenty years, not for its own flaws, but for the authority of whoever opposes it and the political context of whoever proposes it.

repere.texte: In his 1956 article, Knorozov studies about eighty isolated glyphs: days, months, time periods, five colors, four cardinal points, and several signs from Landa's alphabet, for which he proposes a new syllabic reading, presented that same year at the 32nd International Congress of Americanists, in Copenhagen.
repere.source: Youri Knorozov, "New data on the Maya written language," Journal de la Société des Américanistes, vol. 45, 1956, pp. 209-217

carte.punch: In 1952, a Soviet researcher proposes reading Maya glyphs as syllables.
carte.idee: In 1952, Yuri Knorozov reads the Maya "alphabet" recorded by bishop Diego de Landa as a syllabic system, not an alphabetic one. The archaeologist J. Eric S. Thompson opposes him for twenty years. The syllabic reading prevails after 1973, when Palenque's dynasty is reconstructed.

quiz.question: What does Yuri Knorozov propose in 1952 about the Maya "alphabet" recorded by bishop Diego de Landa in the sixteenth century?
choix: That this glossary is an invention with no connection to actual Maya writing
That each sign in it corresponds not to an isolated letter but to a Maya syllable
That Maya writing is made up only of signs standing for whole words, never sounds
That Diego de Landa invented Maya writing himself to make evangelization easier
quiz.explication: Knorozov reads Landa's glossary as a syllabic system: each sign corresponds to a consonant followed by a vowel, and the Maya scribe who dictated it pronounced the sound of the Spanish letter rather than its name. This is neither an invention unrelated to real writing, nor proof of a writing system made only of whole words, nor a fabrication by Landa himself.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Why does Yuri Knorozov think the glossary recorded by Diego de Landa must be read differently from a letter-by-letter alphabet?
choix: Because the Maya scribe, not knowing the Spanish names of the letters, pronounced their sound as a Maya syllable
Because a second manuscript by Landa, discovered in 1952, contradicted the first glossary he had written
Because a stela from Palenque had just been deciphered by other researchers at the time
Because contemporary Maya speakers had themselves reported it to him in an oral interview
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The text explains that the Maya scribe, not knowing the Spanish names of the letters, pronounced the sound each letter makes in Spanish, heard as a Maya syllable. No second manuscript, stela, or oral account is mentioned.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Who opposes Knorozov's syllabic hypothesis for about twenty years?
choix: Tatiana Proskouriakoff, who defends a purely logographic reading
The Moscow Institute of Ethnography, which disavows its own researcher
The British archaeologist J. Eric S. Thompson, whose authority then dominates Maya studies
The International Congress of Americanists, held in Copenhagen in 1956
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The text names J. Eric S. Thompson as the opponent whose authority dominates Maya studies for two decades. Proskouriakoff instead works on the historical stelae, and neither of the other two proposals opposes anything in the text.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What happens in December 1973, at the first Palenque Round Table?
choix: Thompson publicly admits his error and endorses the syllabic reading
A team reconstructs, in a single afternoon, most of the city's dynastic list of kings
Knorozov presents his 1952 hypothesis for the first time before a Western audience
Researchers conclude that Maya writing is entirely logographic
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The text says a team using the syllabic approach reconstructs, in a single afternoon, Palenque's dynastic list. Thompson admits nothing publicly, Knorozov had already presented his hypothesis in 1956, and the writing turned out to be mixed.
